learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected keeps climbing without limit and locked it in.
observations.exploration: At zero time speed was zero. One keyboard step to 5 s gave 35.1 m/s belly down; 40 s gave 43.2 and stated drag matches weight. Switched head down at 40 s, giving 66.0. Home reset to zero and End restored 66.0.
observations.reveal: Corrected to near 43 m/s for the original belly-down case, referenced the observed 43.2 value, explained speed-squared drag and force cancellation, then head-down limit 66. Steady sea-level air and typical drag areas stated.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Saturating curve and equal opposing force arrows visible. Reveal retained head-down 66 curve with dashed previous belly-down curve near 43 and readable model caveat.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Clear qualitative misconception and numerical alternatives are committed before exploration.
prediction.evidence: Unlimited growth chosen against two plateaus.

interaction.reason: Time reset and pose switch isolate growth and drag-area contrast.

payoff.reason: Reveal explains a persistent force without persistent acceleration.
payoff.evidence: Drag grows to match weight and cancels net force.

clarity.reason: Curve and force arrows reinforce the same condition.
clarity.evidence: Plateau and balanced arrows at long time; previous pose dashed.

transfer.reason: Conditional physical mechanism is given, but no new application is attempted.
transfer.evidence: Sea-level model and different drag area pose contrast.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard endpoints worked and values had text summaries; screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Gravity can continue while acceleration stops.
surprise.evidence: Long-time plateau with downward weight still shown.

visualExplanation.reason: Force balance and curve jointly explain the limit.

playfulness.reason: Time scrubber and pose toggle support comparison.
playfulness.evidence: Zero to 40 s and two poses.

depth.reason: Links force balance, quadratic drag and terminal speed.

complexity.reason: Simple graph controls introduce force versus acceleration distinction.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Understand growing drag and net force cancellation while motion continues.
complexity.interfaceBurden: One stepped time slider and a pose toggle.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Drag area, force balance and squared-speed response.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Speed-time graph, m/s, kg and area units.

whyCool: Equal force arrows explain a speed limit without turning gravity off.
caveat: Model assumes steady sea-level air; pose comparison recomputes a fall for that pose, not a real transition trajectory.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
